evidence: Page 16 register definition: "ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED), on the book's teaching geometry". Page 17: "[ILLUSTRATIVE] is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical worked example... [canonical scenario]/[ILLUSTRATIVE] says whether it is the book's fixed reference set or a one-off what-if." and "A vendor hardware constant (e.g. the H100 footprint) is [1P][FACT], never [ILLUSTRATIVE]."
issue: The same named register/tag has two contradictory scopes two pages apart: on p. xii the ILLUSTRATIVE register explicitly includes "[canonical scenario]" inputs, while p. xiii defines the [ILLUSTRATIVE] tag as reserved for non-canonical examples and distinct from [canonical scenario]. A reader cannot tell from p. xii whether a canonical-scenario number belongs inside the ILLUSTRATIVE register.
fix_instruction: Restrict the p. xii register parenthetical to "([ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED)" and describe canonical-scenario inputs in their own register, or explicitly state that the register name and the Axis-1 tag differ in scope.

evidence: Page 17: "the canonical scenario (Ch. 4, Table 4-2) keeps its own [canonical scenario] provenance, and within it the epistemic-status axis splits every value into exactly two cases." Page 90: "Later chapters add hypothesized results — a candidate lever, [HYPOTHESIS], epistemic axis — and validated results, MEASURED, measurement axis... The four states — given → derived → hypothesized → validated — are the log... The three axes are never mixed — Note 1 below."
issue: Two internal tensions in the rule text: (a) the "exactly two cases" rule for canonical-scenario values is contradicted by Table 4-2's own change log, which contemplates the same table's quantities later carrying [HYPOTHESIS] (Axis 2) and MEASURED (Axis 3) — a third case; (b) the four-state log sequence spans Axis 2 (given/derived/hypothesized) and Axis 3 (validated/MEASURED) in one chain, immediately after asserting "The three axes are never mixed".
fix_instruction: Scope the "exactly two cases" rule to Table 4-2's as-printed input/derived rows, and restate the assumption-change log as a lifecycle that legitimately crosses axes (or map 'validated' onto an Axis-2 term) so the never-mixed rule holds as written.

issue: The figure prints "in-flight" for the KV-resident slot count — the exact conflation (in-flight vs KV-resident) Ch 4 spends a full subsection forbidding; the caption acknowledges the error but the figure itself is left uncorrected.

evidence: Page 151 (§7.3.1): "At 9,500 resident tokens, one sequence needs 1.245184 GB of raw KV. With an explicitly assumed 4 GB reserve for runtime state and workspace, the analytical budget is 21.245184 GB. A nominal 24 GB device passes this preliminary capacity gate." (16 GB weights + 1.245184 GB KV + 4 GB reserve = 21.245184 GB.)
issue: Mislabelled quantity: 21.245184 GB is the total analytical footprint (weights + KV + reserve), not a "budget"; the KV budget on a 24 GB device with a 4 GB reserve is 24 − 4 = 20 GB. As written, a reader could read 21.2 GB as space available for KV.
fix_instruction: Rename to "the analytical total footprint is 21.245184 GB" and, if a budget figure is wanted, state the KV budget separately as 20 GB (24 − 4).

evidence: Page 80: "Infrastructure: ≈ $20/hour for an 8×H100 host at $2.50/GPU-hr on-demand [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]; not illustrative 2026 cloud-price input ($2.50/H100-GPU-hour, [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], not a market fact) → $20/hr per 8-GPU node".
issue: Garbled negation: "not illustrative 2026 cloud-price input" reads as denying that the $2.50 figure is a cloud-price input, when the intended meaning (per Table 4-2's parallel note "a dated price snapshot... not [1P] vendor spec, not a measured figure") is presumably "not [ILLUSTRATIVE] — a 2026 cloud-price input". In a load-bearing economic cell this invites misreading of the price's provenance.
fix_instruction: Rewrite as "...[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] — not [ILLUSTRATIVE]; a 2026 cloud-price input, not a market fact → $20/hr per 8-GPU node".
